page: Microsoft Azure D128ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features dedicated x86_64 compute resources powered by Intel Xeon 8573C processors operating up to 4.2 GHz. The hardware layout exposes 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores using two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 512.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The processor architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (VNNI and BF16) alongside Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for matrix math acceleration.

Integrated storage consists of 7,560 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, providing fast, low-latency temporary storage. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight the strength of the 128 vCPU configuration: multi-threaded tests, including PassMark CPU (105,828.49), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (742.86 GB/sec), and stress-ng multi-core (116,506.62), place in the top 10% to top 25%. Instruction-specific benchmarks such as PassMark CPU extended instructions and encryption perform in the top decile due to dedicated cryptographic and vector hardware flags.

Data throughput metrics reinforce high-density capabilities. Memory bandwidth testing shows 511.08 GB/sec uncached read throughput and 219.38 GB/sec write throughput. The instance achieves top-tier results in Redis SET benchmarks (156.93 million ops/sec), static web serving throughput (171.91 GB/sec), and PassMark database operations (35,291.08). Single-thread performance occupies the middle to upper tiers, as shown by stress-ng single-core (1,949.68) and Geekbench single-core (2,134.0), showing that multi-threaded scaling delivers the primary performance benefit.

The large resource scale offers substantial compute and I/O capacity per instance, reducing the overhead of managing multi-node server clusters. With 7,560 GB of local NVMe storage and 512 GB of RAM, it is suited for enterprise relational and in-memory databases, large-scale software compilation, distributed caching tiers, and multi-threaded data engineering jobs.
